Summer values: bermudagrass 3÷5 = 60.0%, zoysiagrass 3.5÷5.5 = 63.6%, Kentucky bluegrass and ryegrass 5÷7 = 71.4%, tall fescue 6÷8 = 75.0%, bentgrass 2÷3 = 66.7%, seashore paspalum 2.5÷4 = 62.5%. map.为什么要遵守一次只剪 1/3 的原则？: Why follow the rule of cutting only 1/3 at a time?
map.一次剪掉超过叶高 1/3 会大量损失光合面积，迫使植株动用根部贮藏养分恢复，抑制: Cutting more than 1/3 of the leaf height at once loses a large photosynthesizing area, forcing the plant to draw on root reserves to recover, inhibiting root growth and inviting bare patches and weed invasion. The correct approach is 'little and often': work at the intervals recommended in the table (warm-season 4-7 days in summer, cool-season 5-10 days, bentgrass 3-5 days) and cut only 1/3 each time. If the lawn has already grown too tall through delay, lower it to the target in 2-3 passes spaced 2-3 days apart.
map.冬季为什么标注停止修剪？: Why is winter marked as stop mowing?
map.表中所有草种冬季频次都标为停止修剪，此时草坪进入休眠或生长极缓，修剪会刺激徒长、: All grass species in the table are marked as stop mowing in winter, when the lawn is dormant or growing very slowly; mowing then stimulates leggy growth, consumes stored nutrients and raises the risk of frost and disease damage. The last mow before winter can be slightly below the normal recommended height (for example 2 cm for bermudagrass, 3 cm for Kentucky bluegrass) to reduce snow mould and thatch build-up, helping overwintering and green-up next year.
